key_provisions_or_claims: AI-driven data and algorithms take deterministic roles in educational policy, evaluation and curriculum.
Synthetic governance (Gulson, Sellar, Webb) blends human and machine decision-making through opaque data infrastructures.
Technical pursuit of control undermines control and deskills teachers.
Critiques the AI dream of human perfectibility as a fascist form of the human.
Proposes Afrofuturist and more-than-human relationships as alternatives.
annotation.summary_en: Curriculum-studies essay critiquing AI chatbots and algorithmic 'synthetic governance' in educational policy, drawing on Bender, Butler and Gulson, Sellar and Webb. It argues datafication undermines teacher expertise and control, and turns to Afrofuturism, a dancing robot art installation and more-than-human relations as alternatives.
annotation.title_clean: Stochastic Parrots, Policies, Octopi Who Pretend to Be Human, & Dancing Robots
